slots.text: Why Memory Matters?

Humans
Learn from past problem-solving
Improve efficiency & accuracy over time
LLM Agents (today)
Do not retain experience
Restart from scratch every query
Era of Experience (Proposed by David Silver, Richard S. Sutton)
Beyond simulation & human data
Agents that remember, adapt, and improve with use
“The era of experience marks a pivotal moment in the evolution of AI. Building on today’s strong foundations but moving beyond the limitations of human-derived data, agents will increasingly learn from their own interactions with the world. Agents will autonomously interact with environments through rich observations and actions. They will continue to adapt over the course of lifelong streams of experience. Their goals will be directable towards any combination of grounded signals.”
Figure: Evolution of AI — from Simulation & Human Data to the Era of Experience

Mainstream Architectures (1): Vector Database-Based Information Retrieval & Generation
Principle
Retrieve external knowledge (docs, DBs) → generate with context
Combines information retrieval + language modelling
Workflow
User inputs query q
Embedding retriever finds similar docs D(q) (e.g., FAISS)
LM generates response using [q, D(q)]
Representative Systems
RAG (Facebook, 2020)
LoCoMo (Snap, 2024)
Emerging: DeepRetriever (2025) → better query–doc matching
Pros
Scalable
Knowledge easily updata

Problem Formulation
Setting:
Multi-session dialogues
Facts spread across distant turns
External memory needed for QA
Goal:
Adaptive memory management (Memory Manager)
Selective memory utilization (Answer Agent)
Core Challenge:
Go beyond heuristics & fixed top-k retrieval
RL to optimize memory ops & answer correctness
Questions can only be answered with information from the dialogues

Exact Match (EM) reward → more balanced across F1, BLEU-1, and J
Trade-off insight: choosing reward function impacts model behaviour
- optimizing for semantic richness vs precision and conciseness
RL Algorithm Comparison:
GRPO converges faster than PPO

Answer Agent Synergy:

LLM-as-Judge reward → higher J score but generates longer, verbose answers

Limitations & Future work
Limitations
Benchmarks (e.g., LOCOMO) limited in scale & diversity
No dataset for evaluating memory ops {ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP}
System depends on QA supervision
Supports only one memory type (no separation of episodic, semantic, procedural, etc.)
Text only (no multimodal support yet)
Future Work
Build memory-centric datasets
Incorporate different memory types (episodic, semantic, procedural, and etc.)
Extend to multimodal memory (text + images + audio)
Apply to r
